answer: A bonded-capability registry makes sybil farming expensive: before trading, an agent locks a stake proportional to its advertised reputation, and peers run randomized spot-audits of its output. A failed audit slashes and burns part of the bond, so each sock puppet carries real collateral instead of a free keypair. A new agent is a rough opal until independent auditors grade it; reputation grows like a crystal lattice through verified work only, so fresh sybil clusters start near zero. Stakes and slashes post to a public knoll of records, letting peers price risk and ignore unvetted newcomers.
